_about: The server's access rules for POST /api/v1/vaults/{vaultId}/log (design 2026-11-15-onboarding-trust §3.7, FC-1; spec 03 §10.3 and §10.4). Server-only: the JVM suite grades it, no client does.
Hand-authored from the independent oracle in tools/vector-gen/oracle (Node WebCrypto and @noble; no andvari code). Regenerate with `npm run generate` there; `npm run check` fails on any difference.

A row: the vault `vaultId` holds the chain `chains[stored]` (frames in order; `none` is a vault id nobody has used); the server's grant table is `chains[stored].grants`; `chains[stored].purged` says whether the vault's grace period has ended and the server purged it (the log is kept with the tombstone); the account `caller` posts `frameB64` as `entry`; `expect` is the wire answer. `entry`, where present, is the parsed statement, for reading.

expect: { status, error } for a refusal. A log_head_moved answer carries the stored head as seq, hash and at; NO other answer carries a head, and no_grant in particular never does. { status: 200, appended } for a success: appended true means the entry was stored at the head plus one, and `grantsAfter` is then the grant table after its effect; appended false is the retry answer, a 200 that changes nothing.

grants: one row per account that has ever held a grant: { userId, role, revokedBy }. revokedBy is null for an active grant, or the kind of the entry that revoked it: "delete" (the revocation the design calls reason vault_delete), "leave" or "remove". The server's own reason names are not graded. A harness that builds the state by posting the chain's frames in order, each as its actor, can assert this table.

The checks, in the design's order. Step 3: the strict parse and purpose 0x03 (bad_frame, also for unknown_format; non_canonical; bad_statement), then the frame's vaultId against the path (wrong_vault). Step 4: the actor is the caller and the signer maps to the caller's stored identity key (bad_signer), then the signature (bad_signature). Step 5: a frame byte-identical to a stored one answers 200 before any grant check; a genesis needs an unused vault id (409 vault_id_taken); every other kind needs the caller's grant (403 no_grant, also for an unknown vault), where a grant revoked by the vault's delete counts for restore and delete by the owner and for leave, a grant revoked for any other reason never counts, and after the purge no grant counts at all (every append but a genesis is 403 no_grant, the owner's restore included; the retry of a stored frame is still 200); then the role must allow the kind (403 not_vault_owner: add, role, remove, offer, delete and restore need owner). Step 6: seq and prev are the stored head plus one (409 log_head_moved). Step 7: the shared verifier, whose not_authorized is 403 not_vault_owner and whose precondition is 400 precondition.

Outside this file: the session and the body caps with the side data a kind takes (the harness sends well-formed metaBlob, wrappedVk and grant where the kind needs them), the rate buckets, and step 8. Every row is built to pass step 8: the server's clock is `now`, every stored `at` is before it, every posted `at` is at it or earlier, the stored offer expires after it, and every account of the cast is active, connected to the owner and under its limits.

none.why: No vault has this id: nothing is stored.

live.why: alice created the vault and added bob as writer and carol as reader.

deleted.why: live, then the owner deleted the vault: every grant is revoked by the delete, and the vault is in its grace period.

purged.why: deleted, and the grace period has ended: the server purged the vault and keeps its row as a tombstone with the log. The chain is the same four entries.

left.why: live, then bob left: his own entry revoked his grant.

declined.why: alice created the vault and added bob; bob declined, which signs a leave.

removed.why: live, then the owner removed bob.

readded.why: removed, then the owner added bob again.

left-in-grace.why: deleted, then bob left during the grace period: his revocation is no longer the delete's.

restored-after-a-leave.why: left-in-grace, then the owner restored the vault: the restore re-granted carol and skipped bob.

offered.why: live, then the owner offered the vault to bob for 7 days.

transferred.why: offered, then bob accepted: bob is the owner and alice a writer.

rows.name: owner-adds-a-member
rows.why: The owner appends an add at the stored head plus one.

rows.name: member-leaves
rows.why: A member appends its own leave: any member may. The entry's effect revokes its grant.

rows.name: genesis-creates-the-vault
rows.why: A genesis for an unused vault id: there is no vault and no grant to resolve.

rows.name: retried-add
rows.why: A frame byte-identical to one already stored, posted again by its actor: 200, and nothing changes. The stored frame need not be the head.

rows.name: retried-genesis
rows.why: The stored genesis posted again by its creator: the retry rule comes before the genesis rule, so this is 200, not vault_id_taken.

rows.name: retried-delete
rows.why: A retried byte-identical delete: 200, although the delete revoked the owner's own grant.

rows.name: retried-leave
rows.why: A retried leave whose own effect revoked the caller's grant: 200, before any grant check.

rows.name: retried-decline
rows.why: A decline is a leave. Its retry gets the same 200.

rows.name: retried-leave-in-grace
rows.why: The retry of a leave that was appended during the grace period.

rows.name: retried-leave-after-the-restore
rows.why: The same stored leave posted again after the owner restored the vault: still a byte-identical stored frame from its actor.

rows.name: stored-frame-posted-by-another-account
rows.why: A stored frame posted by an account that is not its actor. The retry rule needs actor = the caller, which step 4 checks first: bad_signer, and a non-member learns nothing.

rows.name: non-member-post
rows.why: A non-member posts an entry at the right position: no_grant, with no head in the answer. (The verifier would say precondition; it is never reached.)

rows.name: non-member-post-at-a-stale-position
rows.why: A non-member posts at a position that is not the head plus one. Access (step 5) comes before position (step 6), so the answer is no_grant and carries no head: a non-member never learns it.

rows.name: non-member-posts-an-owner-kind
rows.why: A non-member posts an add as itself: the grant is resolved before the role, so no_grant, not not_vault_owner.

rows.name: unknown-vault
rows.why: An entry other than a genesis for a vault id that does not exist: no_grant, the same answer a non-member gets.

rows.name: removed-member-posts
rows.why: bob was removed. A grant revoked for any reason but the vault's delete never counts.

rows.name: removed-member-posts-at-a-stale-position
rows.why: The removed member at a stale position: still no_grant, and no head.

rows.name: resigned-leave
rows.why: bob's leave is stored. He signs ANOTHER leave (a new `at`) instead of re-posting the same bytes: it is not a retry, and his grant is revoked by his own leave.

rows.name: readded-member-leaves
rows.why: bob was removed and added again: the add re-activated his grant.

rows.name: writer-adds
rows.why: A writer posts an add: the caller has a grant, but its role does not allow the kind.

rows.name: reader-deletes
rows.why: A reader posts a delete.

rows.name: writer-restores-a-live-vault
rows.why: A writer posts a restore on a vault that is not deleted: its grant is active, so the role decides. Compare non-owner-restores-while-deleted.

rows.name: owner-restores-a-deleted-vault
rows.why: The owner's grant is revoked by the delete; it counts for restore. The restore re-grants every grant still revoked by the delete.

rows.name: second-different-delete
rows.why: A second delete with another deleteId, at the head plus one. The owner's revoked grant counts for delete, the position is right, and the shared verifier refuses it: the vault is already deleted.

rows.name: resigned-delete-at-the-stored-position
rows.why: The owner re-signs its delete with a new `at` for the position the stored delete holds: not a retry (other bytes), and another entry at a stored position is log_head_moved, with the stored head.

rows.name: member-leaves-in-the-grace-period
rows.why: A member's grant revoked by the delete counts for leave. Appending it rewrites the revocation, so a later restore skips this member (FI-R7).

rows.name: reader-leaves-in-the-grace-period
rows.why: The same for the reader.

rows.name: non-owner-restores-while-deleted
rows.why: A grant revoked by the delete counts for restore only when it is the owner's. A writer's does not count: no_grant, not not_vault_owner.

rows.name: non-owner-deletes-while-deleted
rows.why: The same for a delete by a non-owner.

rows.name: owner-adds-while-deleted
rows.why: The owner's revoked grant counts for restore and delete, and for no other owner kind: an add on a deleted vault is no_grant. (The verifier would say precondition; access comes first.)

rows.name: owner-restores-with-another-delete-id
rows.why: A restore that names another deleteId than the stored delete: the grant counts, the verifier refuses.

rows.name: non-member-post-on-a-deleted-vault
rows.why: A non-member's post on a deleted vault.

rows.name: owner-restores-after-a-leave-in-grace
rows.why: bob left during the grace period. The restore re-grants carol and the owner; bob stays out.

rows.name: leaver-stays-out-after-the-restore
rows.why: After the restore, the member who left in the grace period has no grant.

rows.name: other-member-is-back-after-the-restore
rows.why: carol, whose grant the restore re-activated, posts as a member again.

rows.name: owner-restores-after-the-purge
rows.why: The grace period has ended and the vault is purged. Every append other than a genesis is refused with no_grant, the owner's restore included: the exception for a grant revoked by the delete holds only before the purge. Compare owner-restores-a-deleted-vault.

rows.name: member-leaves-after-the-purge
rows.why: A member's leave after the purge: no_grant. Compare member-leaves-in-the-grace-period.

rows.name: owner-deletes-after-the-purge
rows.why: A second delete after the purge: no_grant, where before the purge it was precondition.

rows.name: non-member-post-after-the-purge
rows.why: A non-member's post on a purged vault: the same no_grant.

rows.name: retried-delete-after-the-purge
rows.why: A byte-identical retry of a stored frame after the purge: the retry rule comes first and changes nothing, so it is still 200.

rows.name: genesis-for-a-purged-vault-id
rows.why: A vault id is never reused: a genesis for the id of a purged vault is vault_id_taken, as for a live one.

rows.name: genesis-for-a-vault-id-in-use
rows.why: Another account posts a genesis for a vault id that exists.

rows.name: resigned-genesis
rows.why: The creator signs a NEW genesis (another `at`) for its own vault id: other bytes, so not a retry.

rows.name: member-at-a-stale-position
rows.why: The owner posts at the position the stored head already holds: log_head_moved with the stored head {seq, hash, at}. Compare non-member-post-at-a-stale-position.

rows.name: member-ahead-of-the-head
rows.why: seq is the head plus two.

rows.name: member-with-another-prev
rows.why: seq is the head plus one, but prev is not the stored head's hash.

rows.name: add-of-a-member
rows.why: The owner adds an account that is already a member: the verifier's precondition.

rows.name: accept-without-an-offer
rows.why: A member posts an accept while no offer is pending.

rows.name: at-before-the-head
rows.why: `at` is earlier than the stored head's: `at` never decreases along a log.

rows.name: owner-leaves
rows.why: The owner posts a leave: any member may post the kind, and the verifier refuses the owner's.

rows.name: target-accepts
rows.why: The offer's target accepts: the old owner's grant becomes writer and the target's becomes owner.

rows.name: target-cancels
rows.why: The offer's target cancels it.

rows.name: owner-cancels
rows.why: The owner cancels its offer.

rows.name: bystander-cancels
rows.why: A member who is neither the owner nor the target posts a cancel. Any member may post the kind, so step 5 passes; the verifier says not_authorized, which reaches the wire as not_vault_owner.

rows.name: bystander-accepts
rows.why: A member who is not the target posts an accept: the verifier's not_authorized, as not_vault_owner.

rows.name: old-owner-adds-after-the-transfer
rows.why: alice handed the vault to bob: her server-side role is writer now.

rows.name: new-owner-adds-after-the-transfer
rows.why: The new owner adds a member.

rows.name: genesis-naming-another-owner-key
rows.why: A genesis signed by the caller that names another account's key as ownerKey. Steps 4 to 6 pass; the verifier wants the genesis signed by its own ownerKey: not_authorized, as not_vault_owner.

rows.name: frame-of-another-purpose
rows.why: A frame of another purpose than 0x03.
rows.entryNote: the vault-log statement framed and signed under purpose 0x04

rows.name: frame-with-another-magic
rows.why: unknown_format reaches the wire as bad_frame.
rows.entryNote: the entry with format byte 0x03 in its magic

rows.name: frame-truncated
rows.why: A frame shorter than the shortest frame.
rows.entryNote: the first 60 bytes of the entry

rows.name: statement-not-canonical
rows.why: A statement that is not canonical.
rows.entryNote: the entry signed with a space after a colon

rows.name: statement-version-3
rows.why: A canonical statement with another v.

rows.name: entry-for-another-vault
rows.why: The frame names another vault than the path.

rows.name: actor-is-not-the-caller
rows.why: bob posts an entry whose actor is alice (her valid next entry, never stored).

rows.name: signed-with-another-key
rows.why: The actor is the caller, but the frame is signed with another account's key: the signer does not map to the caller's stored identity key.

rows.name: signature-does-not-verify
rows.why: The actor and the signer key are the caller's; the signature does not verify.

rows.name: order-signer-before-signature
rows.why: An actor that is not the caller, and a broken signature: bad_signer comes first.

rows.name: order-frame-before-access
rows.why: A non-member posts a frame that is not canonical: step 3 comes before step 5.
rows.entryNote: a non-member's leave signed with a space after a colon

rows.name: order-vault-before-signer
rows.why: Another vault in the frame, and an actor that is not the caller: wrong_vault comes first.

rows.name: order-signer-before-access
rows.why: A non-member posts the owner's entry: step 4 comes before step 5, so bad_signer, not no_grant.
